title: Public API stability
description: Keep released APIs compatible, and change them on purpose.

rules.title: API is a contract
rules.text: Treat the public API of a released major version as a compatibility contract. Renames, removals and signature changes need an explicit maintainer decision.

rules.title: Prefer additive changes
rules.text: Prefer additive changes. Add new parameters as optional or keyword-only with safe defaults.

rules.title: Deprecate first
rules.text: Deprecate before removing: keep a working shim and mark it deprecated with the replacement and the removal version.

rules.title: Explicit public surface
rules.text: Define the public surface explicitly, such as __all__ or an exports map. Adding a symbol there is an API decision, not a convenience.

rules.title: Mark internals
rules.text: Mark internals with underscore names or internal entry points so users do not depend on them.

rules.title: No unasked aliases
rules.text: Do not add backward-compatibility re-exports or aliases unless asked.

rules.title: Stable wire formats
rules.text: Never change serialized formats, error codes or protocol field names without a versioned migration path.

rules.title: Types are API
rules.text: Treat exported types as API. Narrowing an accepted type or widening a returned one can break callers.

rules.title: Codemods for majors
rules.text: Ship a codemod or a migration guide with each major release that breaks users.

rules.title: Docs in the same PR
rules.text: Update reference docs and migration notes in the same PR as a public API change.

rules.title: Narrow backports
rules.text: Backport only critical bug fixes and security fixes to maintenance branches, and label them as backports.
